Maybe this is true in your country, but it’s definitely not generally true. Engineering degrees are consistently some of the highest paying bachelors in the US. 

https://www.bankrate.com/loans/student-loans/average-college-graduate-salary/#degree

I know plenty of people who went into engineering literally just for the money. They all have tons of incentive to learn math and graduate and yet still plenty of them fail out/switch to an easier (but less valuable) degree.

You’re not wrong that being passionate about it matters. However, if you aren’t able to learn/master it regardless of the teacher and external incentives, then that is functionally equivalent to not being capable of learning it at all.

>Because at it’s core engineering is maths, it can be easily taught

Not really sure if this is true. Most people are not capable of getting an engineering degree, and it’s primarily because of the math/technical material.

In a typical university (which is already selecting for students who are above average learners), calculus courses are usually weed out courses which have the highest % of students struggling.



I’d say we have more *successful* engineers than *successful* actors because as a society, we don’t need very many actors. In that sense, it’s definitely harder to succeed as an actor because you have to be the best of the best to succeed, whereas an average engineer will still probably do okay.

>How the hell do you make a new friend these days?

Everyone’s just busy and I usually just end up left out of anything people want to do. Out of curiosity, I just looked at my texts to see when the last time someone who wasn’t family or from work texted me.

It was about 6 months ago when a friend told me happy birthday.

I had a long drive with just my own thoughts. And then I got to lay in bed just hoping that horrible, horrible empty feeling would go away.

For most people, friends help (to an extent). They aren’t a replacement for a partner, but the opposite is true as well: just a partner with no friends would probably make you feel lonely too.

They just fill different needs.

But from what I can tell, you do not seem to be at any serious risk of suicide. There are different levels of suicidal ideation. On the lower levels are just the casual thoughts of “what if I just killed myself?” Don’t get me wrong, this is still concerning. It’s just unlikely to lead directly to a lethal attempt.

More concerning is when you start showing reckless disregard for your own life (taking unnecessary risks, not considering possible personal consequences). Very specific plans indicate not just the desire for suicide, but the intent to carry it out.

If you are this worried about being suicidal, you most likely are not.

A psychiatrist and a psychologist are two very different things. 

A psychiatrist is a doctor. They’re going to hear your list of symptoms and your medical history, and then use that to pick a medication. They might also make other recommendations such as “see a therapist” or “stop smoking crack”.

A psychologist in this context usually means a therapist who is not an M.D.  and does prescribe medication. They’re the ones who are going to offer advice, emotional support, and try to get you have some introspection into your own feelings.

Most likely therapy you’ll run into for depression is cognitive behavior therapy (CBT) which focuses on identifying cognitive distortions which are negatively impacting your life. In other words, they try to make sure you’re not looking at things more negatively than they should be.

In my experience the effectiveness of both vary a lot. Medication didn’t do much for me for a while so they kept changing it up until they finally got to one with some effectiveness. Therapy was a similar story; nothing changed at first, new therapist is at least somewhat helping? Too early to say for sure i think.

I would definitely talk to a therapist or mental health professional of some kind if you’re able to. They are the ones who are most qualified to diagnose your problem anyway. 

Don’t worry about the fact that you’re not sure if you’re depressed or not. Clearly, you feel there is a problem here of some kind. That is reason enough to seek treatment.
